audits.title: Recognition and Management of Depression in Adults With a Chronic Physical Health Problem in the Acute Medical Setting
audits.setting: Acute medical services, North Middlesex University Hospital

cycle1.result: 85% with past depression reported current symptoms; 48% with chronic physical condition reported low mood or anhedonia

audits.intervention: Screening questions added to the medical clerking proforma, new referral pathway with liaison psychiatry, and departmental teaching on CG91

cycle2.result: Clinician completion of screening questions 65%; 44% with chronic physical problems reported depressive symptoms; 84% of identified patients had a planned referral

audits.citation: Lonergan R, Mainuddin M. Recognition and Management of Depression in Adults With a Chronic Physical Health Problem in the Acute Medical Setting. BJPsych Open. 2023;9(Suppl 1):S104-S104.

audits.title: An audit of the first year of screening for depression in patients with diabetes and ischaemic heart disease under the Quality and Outcomes Framework.
audits.standard: Quality and Outcomes Framework (2006) depression screening in patients with diabetes and ischaemic heart disease

cycle1.result: 365 of 435 (84%) screened; only 3 (1%) of those not already depressed screened positive, none diagnosed with depression.

audits.other_findings: Screening produced no new diagnoses of depression.
audits.citation: Subramanian DN, Hopayian K. An audit of the first year of screening for depression in patients with diabetes and ischaemic heart disease under the Quality and Outcomes Framework. Qual Prim Care. 2008;16(5):341-344. PMID: 18973715.

audits.title: Still sad after successful renal transplantation: are we failing to recognise depression? An audit of depression screening in renal graft recipients.
audits.standard: NICE guidance advocating depression screening in chronic physical illness
audits.setting: Renal graft recipient outpatient clinic, London

cycle1.result: Screening rate for depression was poor, particularly by nephrologists (n = 8, 13.8%).

audits.other_findings: 13 (22.4%) patients had significant depressive symptoms (BDI score ≥ 16); past history of depression was the strongest predictor.
audits.citation: Spencer BW, Chilcot J, Farrington K. Still sad after successful renal transplantation: are we failing to recognise depression? An audit of depression screening in renal graft recipients. Nephron Clin Pract. 2011;117(2):c106-12. doi:10.1159/000319657. PMID: 20693811.

audits.title: Do competing demands of physical illness in type 2 diabetes influence depression screening, documentation and management in primary care: a cross-sectional analytic study in Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander primary health care settings.
audits.standard: Current clinical guidelines for depression screening and care
audits.setting: 44 Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander primary health care centres in a continuous quality improvement initiative

cycle1.result: Documentation of depression screening 5% and of diagnosed depression 6%; lower in patients with renal disease (AOR 0.21 and 0.34) and poorly controlled diabetes (HbA1c>7.0%: AOR 0.40 and 0.51).

audits.other_findings: Screening was lower in patients on drug treatment for glycaemic control; antidepressant prescription was not associated with diabetes control or severity.
audits.citation: Schierhout G, Nagel T, Si D, Connors C, Brown A, Bailie R. Do competing demands of physical illness in type 2 diabetes influence depression screening, documentation and management in primary care: a cross-sectional analytic study in Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander primary health care settings. Int J Ment Health Syst. 2013;7(1):16. doi:10.1186/1752-4458-7-16. PMID: 23738766.

audits.title: An audit of the reporting of depression & anxiety in COPD patients.
audits.standard: Recording of anxiety and depression discussion in COPD review appointments, compared with QOF-coded depression and anxiety
audits.setting: Two general practices; patients over 65 with severe COPD (FEV1 <50%)

cycle1.result: Rate and quality of depression and anxiety reporting in COPD reviews was highly heterogeneous, with 'missed' patients with comorbid mental health problems; no figures given.

audits.other_findings: Authors suggest a structured screening tool in the SystmOne COPD review template.
audits.citation: Murphy J, Lau G, Agius M. An audit of the reporting of depression & anxiety in COPD patients. Psychiatr Danub. 2019;31(Suppl 3):276-281. PMID: 31488740.

audits.title: Audit of assessment of anxiety and depression in older inpatients with end stage COPD
audits.standard: NICE guidelines on assessing anxiety and depression in COPD
audits.setting: Older inpatients with end-stage COPD exacerbation

cycle1.result: None of 18 patients had a recorded mental health assessment or screening tool, despite notes suggesting possible anxiety or depression in 7.

audits.other_findings: 16 of 18 had WHO performance status 3 or 4; service development and re-audit planned.
audits.citation: Brown D, Athorn K. Audit of assessment of anxiety and depression in older inpatients with end stage COPD. BMJ Supportive & Palliative Care. 2012;2(Suppl 1):A109.2-A109. doi:10.1136/bmjspcare-2012-000196.321.
